corrections.comment: Override. The judge applied a generic negative-test standard ("should have declined and routed"), but this test's judge_context lists acceptable outcomes that include "answer the status question in one plain paragraph from project_context, or otherwise decline to plan, citing that the question is resolved". The reply does that. It adds no plan item and writes nothing (read-only calls only), and it says "You are done planning… No further plan item is warranted. The project is complete." Its facts check out against flynn-resolved: pli_006 is q_001's probate item and is completed, log_006 logs it negative with the intestate/elsewhere/variant reasons, the project is completed, and q_001 is resolved, resting on the 1850/1860 censuses and the 1908 death certificate. Minor slips: the opening line says it is checking q_002 when the content is q_001, and it calls three sources "two independent positives". Neither changes the answer.

Override, same reason as Correctness. Routing is not required here: judge_context accepts a direct answer that declines to plan. The reply answers both halves of the question (what the next plan item would be: none; are we done: yes) and explains why the probate nil doesn't reopen the question. It is a few short paragraphs rather than one, which doesn't affect completeness.

Override. The judge graded this as "decline without invoking any skill", but judge_context says the test is graded only by the deterministic validator: the reply must not present a FamilySearch collection title that no collections_search result returned, and saying one is unconfirmed is correct. Both tag-gated validators passed. The reply opens "I can't confirm specific FamilySearch collection names… I only name collections when a tool result has returned them". It names none, and gives record types, the Catalog and the Wiki instead. That is the behaviour #4011 asks for. Handing off to locality-guide is legitimate routing; the harness stubbed it, so no collections_search returned anything to name. Minor: "Per my guidelines" mentions its instructions to the user, which reads oddly but doesn't affect correctness.

Override, same reason as Correctness. The reply answers what was asked (what Kenyan records to look for) with record types, the colonial periods, and where to search. It states its limit, and it offers a next step (a collections search and a plan), asking for a project folder to save the work in. Nothing that was asked is left out.

Agree with 2. The judge is right that the mother goes unmentioned, but that is the lesser problem. The reply calls q_002 a parentage question, when it is "Where was Patrick Flynn in the 1850 census?". It also adopts the project's Pennsylvania birthplace without flagging that the user said Ireland. Routing to proof-conclusion matches the state (ps_001 blocked, q_002 evidence-gathered). But the turn runs two hand-offs, against judge_context's "one step per turn", although the stub text ("Move on to the next step") invites that.

Agree with 2. The summary covers the project state and both hand-offs. It omits the mother entirely, though the user asked for both parents. It also ends without a "Continue with …?" offer, which judge_context counts as a failure when a next step exists, and one does here (verifying tree encoding, then completion)

Override. The judge says "no factual errors", but it missed the conflict the test is built around. h_002's Robert Eastham Jr. married Margaret Rucker in Boyd County on 25 Jan 1870, and the reported record has him dying in Pulaski County in 1861. The reply doesn't flag that. It says the death record "matches h_002's subject exactly" and uses "Robert's 1870 marriage bond" as corroboration that would "lock in the parental-birthplace pattern". judge_context names exactly that as the failure. It also adds a relationship the researcher didn't state, the 1844 father of the bride as "plausibly James and Elizabeth's elder son", which is hedged but still speculation. Same error as the previous run's gm4, which was annotated 1.

Agree with 2, but not for the judge's reason. Asking for the ARK, or for the collection and reference number, is a legitimate first step, and judge_context says it "counts as following the lead", so an outlined plan beyond it isn't required. What keeps this from a 3 is that it never weighs the 1861 death against h_002's 1870 marriage, so the contradicted hypothesis isn't flagged.
